checkpoint.description: The upper walkway after the high-platform climb, before the next forward guard.

forward_guard.description: The sword input clears the guard and the player continues across the upper walkway.

post_guard_edge.description: Past the upper walkway edge, the player enters a non-landing terrain band and falls into the lower/death area; no scene transition occurs.

windows.description: The player walks across the upper walkway while the ROM keeps the grounded response state.
The edge blocks horizontal progress; local PLAYER_X retreats while world X remains fixed.
Horizontal motion resumes at the edge.
The player leaves the landing state and the vertical integrator begins increasing PLAYER_VY by 0x003C per frame.
The next special terrain behavior is observed during the initial descent, but it does not establish a landing.
The player continues through the open lower band without a supporting surface.
The lower/death-band response stops the fall; the scene remains state 0x01.

debugger.description: The targeted run repeatedly executes the terrain/vertical path and reaches the lower stop without entering the scene transition path.

terrain_context.description: The relevant map column contains special behavior cells, but the controller trace does not produce a landing state on the forward route.

behavior_0x47_interaction.effect: Tests 0x00FFF0BD; a set flag takes the clear-surface-mode path, while a clear flag can arm 0x00FFF0C2 and set the surface-mode bit.

observed: Upper-edge behavior 0x86 dispatches to 0x001B5440 and leaves 0x00FFF0BD clear.
Initial descent behavior 0x85 dispatches to 0x001B5448 and sets 0x00FFF0BD to 0xFF.
No scene-state write or exit-gate write occurs in this run.

special_surface_handlers.conclusion: The 0x85/0x86 pair is a surface-contour flag path used by terrain handling, not a scene transfer. The upper edge remains a fall into the lower/death band unless another route reaches a supporting surface.

next_action: Trace the next playable route from the upper checkpoint or return to the lower wall/rope branch; the 0x85/0x86 edge path is decoded and is not a natural exit.
